newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees up to 35 pct hike in '97 mango exports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees up to 35 pct hike in '97 mango exports.

text.p: Mexico's mango exports could jump up to 35 percent this year from 1996 exports of more than 36.6 million five-kg boxes, Empacadores de Mango de Exportacion (Emex) said Tuesday.

Mango exports "have seen a general tendency from 20 to 35 percent" higher than last year, the company's general manager Luis Alberto Cruz Garcia told Reuters at the Mexico-European Union Agrobusiness Forum here. Emex represents 66 Mexican packing firms.
Mexico is the world's third-largest mango producer and principal exporter to the United States and Canada. Last year's exports drew $110 million in income, Cruz Garcia said.

Mexican producers and packers are launching a campaign to promote the fruit's trade in the face of growing world-wide export competition, former director of Emex and mango producer Juan Manuel Wong Urrea said.
Most mangoes produced in Mexico are consumed domestically, despite growing exports, he added.
